fields.name: rule_set_name
fields.label: Rule Set Name
fields.sourceQuote: Rule Set Name: The name of the rule set.
fields.notes: List-page column on the Purchase Order Matching Rules page; row is the selection target for Edit/Copy. Selecting a row under this column is the first step of every edit/copy/unlock procedure (edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md: 'select the rule set row under Rule Set Name').

fields.name: in_use
fields.label: In Use
fields.sourceQuote: In Use: Shows if the matching rule set has been applied against any active invoice (Yes) or has not yet applied (No) in the system.
fields.notes: Both values are explicitly enumerated in the same clause, not a completed guess. GATE: a rule set with In Use = Yes cannot be modified in any way; the admin must Copy it first, or unlock it via the Change to Non-PO action (see change_to_non_po_action) which breaks its association to all invoices.

fields.name: associated_policies
fields.label: Associated Policies
fields.sourceQuote: Associated Policies: Shows what Invoice PO policy has been configured to include this PO matching rule set. You select a rule set using the PO Matching Ruleset option in Policies.
fields.notes: Read-only display column showing which Policies (Group 1, already-built page) reference this rule set via the PO Matching Ruleset field there. Outbound dependency only - never re-home PO Matching Ruleset to this page.

fields.name: copy_button
fields.label: Copy
fields.sourceQuote: select an existing rule set under Rule Set Name, and then click Copy.
fields.notes: Only documented way to start a new rule set - there is NO 'New' button attested anywhere in the corpus for this page. Also the prescribed workaround for editing a locked (In Use=Yes) rule set (access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md: 'use the Copy button to create a copy, edit the rule set as needed').

fields.name: rename_button
fields.label: Rename
fields.sourceQuote: click Rename and type a descriptive name for the matching rule set, pressing Enter when you are done.
fields.notes: Renames the auto-generated 'Copy of...' entry produced by Copy.

fields.name: done_button
fields.label: Done
fields.sourceQuote: 3.  Click Done.
fields.notes: Terminal step of the Copy -> Rename -> Done rule-set-creation wizard (Step 1). Distinct from the final rule-set Save at the end of Steps 2/3.

fields.name: edit_button
fields.label: Edit
fields.sourceQuote: On the Purchase Order Matching Rules page, select the rule set, and then click Edit.
fields.notes: Opens the rule set for editing (loosely called 'Purchase Order Matching Set' in edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md: 'Click Edit to open Purchase Order Matching Set.'). Only available when In Use = No; also becomes available again after the Change to Non-PO unlock action (test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md: 'the rule set has a status of No and can be edited using the Edit button'). NOT to be confused with the 'Edit' link inside the Exception Message dialog (see exception_message_field) which edits a saved message, not the rule set.

fields.name: edit_rules_button
fields.label: Edit Rules
fields.sourceQuote: in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules. The Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window appears.
fields.notes: Opens the 'Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window' which contains the Rules and Life to Date tabs. CONTRADICTION - TAB DEPTH: step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md never mentions Edit Rules and instead places the Rules tab one level up ('In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab.'). See contradiction 'tab-depth-rules-life-to-date' below; majority tree (2 of 3 topics) is page > Edit > select rule group > Edit Rules > [Rules | Life to Date]. Also used in Step 4 for condition-based sub-rules ('select the new condition, and then click Edit Rules to specify what should happen').

fields.name: rules_tab
fields.label: Rules
fields.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab.
fields.notes: Corpus type unattested as tab vs. window heading - recorded as 'unknown' rather than guessing. Holds the field-to-field (one-to-one) matching rules, the Tolerance controls, Exception Message, and Allow Submit/Approve. Part of contradiction 'tab-depth-rules-life-to-date'.

fields.name: life_to_date_tab
fields.label: Life to Date
fields.sourceQuote: Click the Life to Date tab, then select the check box next to the rule type to activate using the table below:
fields.notes: Holds the 6-row Life to Date rule-type checkbox table (see life_to_date_rule_type_checkboxes) and the Overage Tolerance controls. Part of contradiction 'tab-depth-rules-life-to-date'.

fields.name: name_field
fields.label: Name
fields.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Rules, type a descriptive name for the new rule in Name.
fields.notes: Names a new named rules group (not the top-level rule set, which is named via Rename in Step 1).

fields.name: life_to_date_rule_type_checkboxes
fields.label: Life to Date rule type
fields.sourceQuote: select the check box next to the rule type to activate using the table below:
fields.notes: LONG CATALOG, INDENTED TABLE TRAP: grep -c '^| ' returns 0 on this file, grep -cP '^\s*\|' returns 22 - the table is nested inside a numbered step. Multiple checkboxes may be selected; each selection reveals its own tolerance controls (Value+Currency or Percentage). CORPUS DEFECT ECHO: create-purchase-order-matching-rules-adb700f9.md (truncated file) independently lists this same rule-type set before its body is cut off ('comparing Gross, Net, Line item total, Line item quantity, if matched against received quantities, and/or Line item tax') - corroborates but is itself incomplete, treat as non-authoritative. LABEL DRIFT: configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md uses 'Matched against Received Quantity' (capability bullet, L27) and 'Match against Received Quantity' (procedure step, L60) for what step-2's canonical table calls 'Match against Received Quantity' - see contradiction 'match-against-received-quantity-label-drift'.

fields.name: tolerance_field
fields.label: Tolerance
fields.sourceQuote: Choose one tolerance:
fields.notes: fieldType left 'unknown' because the corpus never states whether the tolerance choice is presented as a dropdown or a radio group. CONTRADICTION - TWO DOCUMENTED VALUE LISTS FOR THE SAME CONTROL, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: see contradiction 'tolerance-value-list'. Do not pick one list over the other.

fields.name: value_percentage_radio
fields.label: Value or Percentage
fields.sourceQuote: select None, Within, or Custom, and then select Value or Percentage.
fields.notes: Secondary refinement shown after a Tolerance choice other than None. Value = 'Specify a number at or above that at which the rule set will trigger an exception.' Percentage = 'Choose a percent above which the rule set will trigger a flag.' Same pattern used for the Life to Date Overage Tolerance (see overage_tolerance_section) and Amounts and Tolerances generally.

fields.name: currency_field
fields.label: Currency
fields.sourceQuote: Currency: Choose the base currency your company uses. Conversions for alternate currencies used on incoming invoices will be calculated automatically and applied by the system.
fields.notes: Listed as a 4th tolerance option in step-3's reading of the Tolerance contradiction ('Currency: Choose the base currency...'). Underlying exchange-rate activation is NOT a control on this page - it is on by default and configured via the Expense Admin module (see dependencyCandidate 'exchange-rates-off-page'). No enumerated currency list found in the corpus.

fields.name: overage_tolerance_section
fields.label: Overage Tolerance
fields.sourceQuote: In the Overage Tolerance section, select Value or Percentage.
fields.notes: This is the Life to Date tab's tolerance mechanism, distinct from the Rules tab's Tolerance control (tolerance_field) - it is a simple Value/Percentage choice with no None/Within/Custom options documented. Do not conflate with tolerance_field's contradiction. Corroborated (with worked examples but different exact phrasing) by step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md's Step 6: 'Select: Value: ... - AND - Currency ... - OR - Percentage'.

fields.name: exception_message_field
fields.label: Exception Message
fields.sourceQuote: Exception Message: Click Change and add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save.
fields.notes: THE FIFTH DIALOG the recon click tree originally omitted, load-bearing for setting a custom exception message. Reached from the Options/Exception Message area of the Rules tab (or the Life to Date tab, per Step 2). Corroborated by refine-the-rules-include-an-exception-message-c174b2b6.md: 'The Exception Message option is available on the Rules tab and will only display when the user triggers the configured rule.' Contains its own nested Change/New/Edit/Save controls - see change_button and new_button.

fields.name: change_button
fields.label: Change
fields.sourceQuote: Click Change and add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save.
fields.notes: Opens the Exception Message editor/list from the Rules or Life to Date tab. First step of the fifth dialog sequence.

fields.name: new_button
fields.label: New
fields.sourceQuote: add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save.
fields.notes: Creates a new exception message inside the Exception Message editor opened via Change.

fields.name: save_button
fields.label: Save
fields.sourceQuote: 9.  Click Save.
fields.notes: Generic Save control that recurs across this page's procedures: final Save of the rule set (Step 3 ends '9. Click Save.'; Step 2 similarly ends its own tolerance/exception-message configuration and proceeds to Step 3), Save inside the Exception Message editor ('then click Save'), and Save at the end of the condition-based rule group workflow (step-4: 'Click Insert to add any addition conditions, and then click Save when you are done.' and 'Add any additional rules, clicking Update after each new rule to add it to the row, then click Save.'). Consolidated as one control since the corpus never distinguishes it by a different label; context is noted here rather than duplicating the field.

fields.name: allow_submit_approve_checkbox
fields.label: Allow Submit/Approve
fields.sourceQuote: Allow Submit/Approve: Select this check box to allow submission and processing of the invoice even if an exception is triggered.
fields.notes: Located precisely in 'the Options section of the Rules tab' per refine-the-rules-allow-submission-despite-tolerance-9b96d467.md. Cross-directory corroboration in tools-guides/how-to-deal-with-exceptions-using-matching-rules-options-171867ad.md: 'Both options are available to the Invoice administration on the Rules tab when configuring the matching rule set' (the two options being this checkbox and Exception Message).

fields.name: add_button
fields.label: Add
fields.sourceQuote: Click Add to insert this rule into the rows under Rules.
fields.notes: Same-labeled Add button recurs in multiple contexts on this page: inserts a completed field-to-field rule into the Rules list (Step 3, and configure-three-way step 7: '7. Click Add.'); adds a condition-based rule group under a named rules group (step-4: 'Select the named rule group within which the condition-based rule set will be included, then click Add.'); and, in the confirmation-type sub-configuration, adds a new rule condition (match-rules-and-rule-sets-87e69410.md: 'Add a new rule condition by selecting the Rule Set (for example "Default"), and then selecting Add').

fields.name: level_field
fields.label: Level
fields.sourceQuote: Select a value from Level (Header, Vendor, Line Item, Line Item - Receipt), so the matching rule operates for the field(s) you want compared.
fields.notes: GROUNDING LANDMINE: the fourth value is spelled three different ways across the corpus - see contradiction 'level-item-receipt-label-drift'. CONTRADICTION - PARTIAL LIST: tools-guides/match-rules-and-match-status-8cc2c56b.md enumerates only THREE values for the same Rules-type level concept, omitting the fourth - see contradiction 'level-partial-list'. Determines which fields populate the Payment Request and Purchase Order dropdowns (step-3: 'As different levels are chosen in Level, different field sets will populate the selections available in Payment Request and Purchase Order.').

fields.name: payment_request_field
fields.label: Payment Request
fields.sourceQuote: In the Payment Request list, select the request field to match to the same field in the PO.
fields.notes: Populated dynamically based on Level; no enumerated option list found for any Level value (best-practices-129dae61.md gives worked examples like Unit Price, Vendor, Shipping but never states these are the exhaustive list).

fields.name: purchase_order_field_select
fields.label: Purchase Order
fields.sourceQuote: Under Purchase Order, select the PO field to match to the invoice (they will change depending on the field selected in the step above).
fields.notes: Companion dropdown to payment_request_field; also dynamically populated by Level. No enumerated option list found.

fields.name: insert_button
fields.label: Insert
fields.sourceQuote: Click Insert to add any addition conditions, and then click Save when you are done.
fields.notes: Adds another condition row inside the Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions dialog. SAP typo preserved: 'any addition conditions' for 'any additional conditions'.

fields.name: update_button
fields.label: Update
fields.sourceQuote: Click Update to add the rule to the row.
fields.notes: Commits a condition-based rule (created via Edit Rules) into its row within the named rules group; repeat then final Save.

fields.name: delete_button
fields.label: Delete
fields.sourceQuote: delete the rule by selecting and clicking Delete.
fields.notes: Deletes a default or added rule row from the Rules tab. Also documented as an action for a rule condition in the confirmation-type sub-configuration: 'select Edit, Copy, Delete, or Rename to perform those functions' (match-rules-and-rule-sets-87e69410.md).

fields.name: edit_confirmation_button
fields.label: Edit Confirmation
fields.sourceQuote: Do this by clicking Edit Confirmation to open the Select Confirmation Type window, choosing a confirmation type based on the rule group.
fields.notes: Opens the Select Confirmation Type window (confirmation_type_field). Corroborated in match-rules-and-rule-sets-87e69410.md, applied to either the Rule Set itself or a rule condition: 'select an existing Rule Set ("Default") or rule condition ("Services Under $5000"), and then select Edit Confirmation to create or change the confirmation type.'

fields.name: confirmation_type_field
fields.label: Select Confirmation Type
fields.sourceQuote: Concur Invoice provides three confirmation types, with a fourth (None) assigned to those that should not have any text.
fields.notes: Full 4-value list corroborated and numbered in confirmation-types-b4a94761.md ('there are four types: 1. None ... 2. Invoice ... 3. Receipt Central ... 4. Receipt Individual'). Step-5's own table only carries 3 rows (Invoice/INVC, Receipt Individual/RIND, Receipt Central/RCEN) with default message text and Intent because None has no message text to localize - not a contradiction, the two sources agree None is excluded from the message-text table. 'Parent choice' is a documented special state that can appear for rule CONDITIONS only, meaning the parent Rule Set's confirmation-type choice is inherited (match-rules-and-rule-sets-87e69410.md: 'Parent choice displays for rule conditions only, and indicates the choice made for the parent Rule Set will be used.'). GATE: is_receipt_required (Yes on the PO line, set via PO Import, off-page) must be true or no receipt confirmation logic - including this field's outcome - is ever evaluated for that line (is-receipt-required-value-on-po-line-item-896466e1.md).

fields.name: group_conditions_dialog
fields.label: Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions
fields.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions, configure the conditions that the system will detect and then execute the matching rule set on
fields.notes: ONLY ATTESTATION of this dialog name in the corpus. It is where custom field conditions (e.g. vendor = 'Brooks') that make a Named Rules Group into a condition-based sub-rule are configured. No enumerated field/operator/value list is given - thin is correct here. Reached by: select rule set > Edit > select named rule group > Add.

fields.name: default_rule_group_select
fields.label: Default
fields.sourceQuote: Select Default, then click Edit Rules (this named rules group is the basis for your new rules group).
fields.notes: Selects the pre-existing 'Default' named rules group as the starting point for editing; 'Default' also names the default rule set itself elsewhere (create-purchase-order-matching-rules-adb700f9.md: 'A Default rule set is provided'). Corpus does not distinguish whether Default is a row selection or a named entity picker - fieldType left unknown.

fields.name: rule_groups_list
fields.label: Rule Groups
fields.sourceQuote: in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules. The Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window appears.
fields.notes: The selectable list of named rules groups inside an opened rule set. No enumerated membership beyond 'Default' and any condition-based groups the admin has added.

fields.name: change_to_non_po_action
fields.label: Change to Non-PO
fields.sourceQuote: In the Actions menu, click Change to Non-PO.
fields.notes: THE UNLOCK MECHANISM for an In Use=Yes rule set: reclassifying every PO-based invoice associated with the rule set to a non-PO policy (via the Actions menu on the My Invoices page, NOT a control physically on the Purchase Order Matching Rules page itself) breaks the association and flips the rule set's In Use status back to No so Edit becomes available again. CONTRADICTION - LABEL DRIFT: see contradiction 'unlock-action-label'. Full documented sequence per 12786d77.md: My Invoices > select PO-based invoice(s) > Actions menu > Change to Non-PO > Select a Policy window > choose non-PO policy > OK; may also require reassignment via the Assign button if the invoice is unsubmitted and needs a new owner with access to the new policy.

contradictions.topic: Tolerance control value list on the Rules tab (PO-to-Request field / three-way matching rules)

readings.summary: Four values: None, Within (+/-), Custom, Currency.
Three values: None, Within, or Custom (Currency handled as a separate later concept, exchange rates), followed by a separate Value/Percentage choice.
readings.sourceQuote: in the Tolerance section, select None, Within, or Custom, and then select Value or Percentage.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: A driver should probe for exactly these three option labels first (None, Within, Custom) as they agree between both sources, then separately check whether a fourth 'Currency' option is present in the same control or is instead a distinct Value/Percentage/Currency refinement step that follows. Do not assume a 3-item or 4-item list without probing live.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: 'Currency' may not be a sibling tolerance TYPE at all but a label step-3's author folded into the tolerance bullet list because Currency selection (base currency) always co-occurs with a Within/Custom tolerance choice involving cross-currency amounts, whereas configure-three-way-matching treats Currency-selection as happening only after Value/Percentage is chosen. Both topics describe the same underlying Rules-tab Tolerance mechanism for a Line Item-level rule; possibly provisioning- or rule-type-dependent.

contradictions.topic: Click-depth of the Rules and Life to Date tabs relative to the rule set editor

readings.summary: Rules tab is reached ONE level down, directly inside 'Purchase Order Matching Set' (opened by Edit), with no Edit Rules step.
readings.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab.

readings.summary: Both tabs are reached TWO levels down: select rule set > Edit > select a rule group (e.g. Default) > Edit Rules opens the rules window that contains the Rules and Life to Date tabs.
readings.sourceQuote: Select Default, then click Edit Rules (this named rules group is the basis for your new rules group).

readings.summary: Confirms the two-level-down reading: select a rule group and click Edit Rules opens the 'Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window', then the Life to Date tab is clicked from inside that window.
readings.sourceQuote: Click the Life to Date tab, and then select the Match against Received Quantity option.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Drive to the two-level-down tree first (page > select rule set > Edit > select rule group > Edit Rules > [Rules | Life to Date]) since it is corroborated 2-to-1 by both admin-guides step topics that use it, but fall back to a direct Rules-tab click one level up (skip Edit Rules) if the two-level path is not found live - step-3 may simply be describing a route into an already-open editor rather than a full path from the page.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: step-3 may assume the reader is already inside the rule-group rules window from having just completed Step 2 in the same session, and so omits the Edit Rules step as already-done context rather than describing a genuinely shallower click path.
